column3: くろいシャツをきています
column6: くろい|シャツ|を|きて|います
column8: Kiru (ru-verb, to put on upper-body clothing) → kite + imasu. The resulting state is “am wearing.” Kuroi is an i-adjective.

column3: くろいズボンをはいています
column6: くろい|ズボン|を|はいて|います
column8: Haku (u-verb, to put on lower-body clothing or footwear) → haite + imasu = am wearing. Ku → ite makes the te-form.

column3: ちゃいろいくつをはいています
column6: ちゃいろい|くつ|を|はいて|います
column8: Haku → haite imasu is used for shoes as well as pants. Chairoi means brown and is an i-adjective.

column1: Kami ga mijikakute, se ga takai desu.
column2: My hair is short, and I’m tall.
column3: かみがみじかくてせがたかいです
column6: かみ|が|みじかくて|せ|が|たかい|です
column8: Mijikai → mijikakute links “hair is short” to the next description. Se ga takai literally means height is high. Both are i-adjectives.
